I tested it (`results/finite_pop_check.csv`, `analysis/finite_pop_check.py`, METHODS.md section "Finite-population check"; experiment-repo `main`, paper-repo `dev` 0460fb0).
  > 
  > Observed SD of the PPI++ estimate in the disjoint cell relative to the iid cell of the same id, against an approximation from the pool size P and the population σ²_res, V_g (not an exact formula): galaxies (P = 16 743, N = 10⁴) n = 3000: 0.828 observed vs 0.831 predicted (SE/SD 1.21, coverage 0.984 vs 0.950 iid); n = 1000: 0.917 vs 0.939; n = 500: 0.942 vs 0.968; n ≤ 300 ≈ 1 both. gene_expression (P = 61 150) n = 3000: 0.929 vs 0.910. census_income (P = 380 091) has no effect to predict. MC error of an SD ratio at R = 2000 is about ±0.02, so the pattern (SD falls with M/P, the iid-assuming SE then over-covers) is the evidence, not each cell. The text may say the overcoverage is explained by the finite pool, quantitatively consistent with the approximation within MC error at n ≥ 300; it is not a proof. No reply needed.
